newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr/yen seen sustained by short-covering in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen seen sustained by short-covering in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is likely to be supported by short-covering in Asia on Wednesday after an overnight tumble following the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates steady, dealers said.
Although dollar sentiment worsened due to its falls against the mark and other currencies overnight, follow-through selling linked to the interest rate factor is unlikely to emerge here, they said.
"The direction is still downward, but short-covering is likely to take place and this could limit the dollar's falls," said a trust bank dealer.
Expectations that the interest rate gap between Japan and the United States will narrow sharply knocked the dollar down on Monday, with the dollar falling as low as 111.98 yen.

"However, the dollar won't be sold further on these expectations today since there are lingering hopes of an U.S. interest rate rise later this year," said the trust bank dealer. Meanwhile, Japan's low interest rate policy is unlikely to be changed any time soon.
There are fears Japanese investors' hedge selling could push the dollar down further, but the trust bank dealer said hedge sales by trust banks have already hit a peak.
Dealers said Tuesday's remarks by a Japanese official to curb the yen's rapid rise would make operators cautious about selling dollars actively.

Eisuke Sakakibara, the director-general of the Japanese Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau said on Tuesday that the pace of the yen's strengthening against the dollar was too rapid. He added that too much volatility in foreign exchange markets was undesirable and that Japan would "deal appropriately" with such excessive volatility.
A dealer at a city bank said the dollar may rebound as high as 113.50 yen in Tokyo.
The bank dealer said that if a scheduled 10-year Japanese government bond auction on Wednesday goes smoothly and the government bond yield falls, the dollar would be supported.
But dealers said selling interest from Asian central banks and Japanese exporters would likely make the dollar's return to 114 yen difficult.
The dollar is expected to supported against the mark, with solid buying orders seen below 1.6700 marks.
The market is also awaiting the release of U.S. trade data at 1230 GMT.
